_meta.policy: Roadmap is execution order only; parity claims still require checklist dimensions to be complete.

overall.methodology: status-derived average across all services and dimensions

azureFunctionsDurable.methodology: status-derived base plus bounded evidence bonuses from local facade, provider behavior, data-plane status, and green parity pack

logicWorkflows.methodology: status-derived base plus bounded evidence bonuses from local facade, provider behavior, data-plane status, and green parity pack

verifiedPlatformSnapshot.scope: Platform lifecycle evidence: build, lint, unit tests, deployment, provider-lifecycle, ARM readback, integration tests, and cleanup. Runtime/data-plane depth still belongs to service-specific parity packs and future complex platform waves.

crossCuttingBacklog.label: More live Azure capture expansion per service
crossCuttingBacklog.detail: Turn candidate control-plane and data-plane calls into cleanup-verified real Azure fixtures for every high-value service surface.
commands: npm run conformance:classify && npm run conformance:expectations

crossCuttingBacklog.label: More parameter variance beyond generic invalid/missing cases
crossCuttingBacklog.detail: Add service-specific invalid names, parent references, enum values, mutually-exclusive fields, range checks, and schema-shape captures before normalizing local behavior.
commands: npm run conformance:classify && npm run conformance:expectations

crossCuttingBacklog.label: Provider refresh, diff/preview, update, import, drift, and destroy semantics
crossCuttingBacklog.detail: Extend each platform runner beyond create/destroy smoke so generated IaC behaves the same way against GlobalStack as it does against Azure provider tooling.

crossCuttingBacklog.label: Exact error-shape and header fidelity
crossCuttingBacklog.detail: Match Azure status codes, error codes, body structure, async-operation headers, retry headers, and request-id shaped responses for captured cases.
commands: npm run conformance:classify && npm run conformance:expectations

crossCuttingBacklog.label: Retry and eventual-consistency behavior
crossCuttingBacklog.detail: Capture poll cadence, transitional states, delayed reads, delete lag, and retryable failures before claiming timing fidelity.
commands: npm run conformance:classify && npm run conformance:expectations

crossCuttingBacklog.label: RBAC and authorization behavior
crossCuttingBacklog.detail: Expand allow/deny matrices for ARM and service data planes, including propagation lag and inherited-scope behavior where Azure actually enforces it.

crossCuttingBacklog.label: Repeat captures for timing-sensitive behavior
crossCuttingBacklog.detail: Re-capture ambiguous or unstable Azure behavior before encoding it into local expectations, especially delete/read races and async completion windows.
commands: npm run conformance:classify && npm run conformance:expectations

crossCuttingBacklog.label: Deeper service-specific data planes where applicable
crossCuttingBacklog.detail: Broaden bounded local facades and official-emulator integrations for services such as Cosmos, Files, Event Hubs, App Configuration, Key Vault, PostgreSQL, MySQL, and Redis.

crossCuttingBacklog.label: Adversarial new task waves
crossCuttingBacklog.detail: Keep generating new ultra-expert Azure IaC bundles that were not explicitly optimized for the current parity set, then run them through the shipment lifecycle and treat the first surviving mismatch as the next engineering target.

crossCuttingBacklog.label: Real-Azure differential reruns
crossCuttingBacklog.detail: Re-run the same deployment and inspection flows against real Azure and GlobalStack so the parity claim is continuously challenged instead of frozen at one historical capture set.
commands: npm run conformance:classify && npm run conformance:expectations

crossCuttingBacklog.label: Conformance runner completion determinism
crossCuttingBacklog.detail: Harden the real-Azure conformance runner so it exits deterministically after capture and cleanup. Some scoped reruns still write fresh fixtures and then go quiet instead of finishing cleanly.
commands: npm run conformance:classify && npm run conformance:expectations

crossCuttingBacklog.label: Repeated timing and drift checks
crossCuttingBacklog.detail: Keep rerunning timing-sensitive delete/read, async polling, and propagation windows so eventual-consistency assumptions stay tied to current Azure behavior instead of stale fixtures.
commands: npm run conformance:parity && npm run conformance:roadmap

crossCuttingBacklog.label: Treat every surviving mismatch as a product gap
crossCuttingBacklog.detail: Classify each new failure as bundle-generation defect, provider defect, or emulator/runtime parity defect, then convert every true Azure mismatch into an explicit product work item instead of a one-off workaround.

extendedContinuationRoadmap.label: Phase 6: Platform breadth pressure
extendedContinuationRoadmap.objective: Take the same adversarial Azure workloads beyond Pulumi TypeScript so the parity claim is exercised across the full supported IaC platform set instead of one dominant toolchain.
tracks: Run 5-bundle adversarial waves across Terraform HCL and OpenTofu HCL with the same shipment lifecycle bar.
Run 5-bundle adversarial waves across Bicep and ARM JSON with the same service graphs, outputs, and destroy guarantees.
Run 5-bundle adversarial waves across Pulumi Python, Pulumi YAML, and Ansible YAML.
Treat every platform-specific mismatch as either generator defect, runner defect, or emulator parity defect; do not blur them together.
Keep the deep Pulumi-only adversarial runner separate from the platform-aware verified runner until the complex runner is explicitly made platform-aware.
extendedContinuationRoadmap.acceptanceBar: Every supported Azure IaC platform has at least one recent adversarial wave with all bundles green through build, lint, unit-tests, deploy, provider-lifecycle, integration-tests, and destroy.

extendedContinuationRoadmap.label: Phase 7: Mutation and lifecycle depth
extendedContinuationRoadmap.objective: Push beyond create/read/destroy into the update, replacement, import, and rollback paths that usually expose the hardest parity mismatches.
tracks: Add mutation-heavy bundles with phased rollouts, partial replacements, and schema-preserving updates.
Add import/adopt flows where the toolchain binds existing Azure-shaped resources into state.
Add out-of-band drift mutations per service family and verify reconcile behavior, not just drift detection.
Add delete/recreate races and replacement-boundary assertions for child resources and scoped extension resources.
extendedContinuationRoadmap.acceptanceBar: Replacement, refresh, drift-reconcile, import/adopt, and rollback semantics are covered by dedicated adversarial tasks and produce the same qualitative behavior against GlobalStack that the provider expects from Azure.

extendedContinuationRoadmap.label: Phase 8: Runtime and orchestration fidelity
extendedContinuationRoadmap.objective: Deepen the hosted-runtime side of the emulator so Function, Logic, APIM, messaging, and storage/event chains hold up under behavior-first integration tests rather than only ARM reads.
tracks: Stress Functions, Logic Apps, APIM, Event Grid, Service Bus, Event Hubs, Key Vault, and Storage in chained operational flows.
Expand negative-path and no-side-effect assertions for invalid auth, invalid payloads, missing dependencies, and retry exhaustion.
Add fan-out/fan-in, long-running orchestration, and multi-hop event delivery verification where the prompt claims them.
Keep integration tests behavior-first: service existence first, then end-to-end operational flow, then negative-path guarantees.
extendedContinuationRoadmap.acceptanceBar: Runtime-heavy adversarial bundles continue to pass without test relaxations, and any surviving mismatch is traceable to a real Azure behavioral difference or an explicit product gap.

extendedContinuationRoadmap.label: Phase 9: Multi-region, network, and policy stress
extendedContinuationRoadmap.objective: Widen the parity claim across active-active topologies, DNS layering, edge routing, private/public resolution, and identity or policy propagation under nested scopes.
tracks: Generate more active-active and east/west or hub/spoke bundles with Front Door, Application Gateway, Load Balancer, public DNS, and private DNS together.
Stress split-horizon DNS, private link style registration, and repeated resolution after link/delete or failover mutations.
Exercise user-assigned identities, RBAC inheritance, and activity-log or metrics-based governance in the same bundles.
Add policy and security surfaces where denial or attachment timing can diverge from naive CRUD assumptions.
extendedContinuationRoadmap.acceptanceBar: Multi-region and policy-heavy adversarial tasks can mutate, refresh, and destroy cleanly while preserving Azure-shaped routing, resolution, and governance behavior.

extendedContinuationRoadmap.label: Phase 10: Real-Azure canary and drift lane
extendedContinuationRoadmap.objective: Keep the `100%` claim honest by repeatedly challenging it against live Azure instead of freezing it at one historical capture set.
tracks: Run narrow, high-signal real-Azure reruns for timing-sensitive, retry-sensitive, and propagation-sensitive service surfaces.
Keep differential checks focused enough to complete cleanly and emit deterministic fixtures.
Record semantic drift only; discard timestamp, request-id, and dynamic endpoint churn unless it reflects real product behavior.
Convert every surviving semantic mismatch into a product work item immediately, with no temporary relaxations.
defaultCommands: npm run conformance:classify && npm run conformance:expectations
npm run conformance:parity && npm run conformance:roadmap
extendedContinuationRoadmap.acceptanceBar: Scoped real-Azure reruns remain part of the default engineering loop, and the roadmap stays synchronized with any live drift or newly surfaced product gap.

immediateNextWork.label: Run the verified 5-bundle wave against Terraform HCL
immediateNextWork.why: Terraform HCL has no complete recorded 5-bundle platform wave yet, so platform breadth is still not fully proven.

immediateNextWork.label: Enable and run the verified 5-bundle wave for Pulumi TypeScript
immediateNextWork.why: Pulumi TypeScript has no complete recorded 5-bundle platform wave yet. Add the five standard platform-wave bundle entries before running the verified wave; the older single-bundle smoke is not enough evidence.

immediateNextWork.label: Enable and run the verified 5-bundle wave for Pulumi YAML
immediateNextWork.why: Pulumi YAML has no complete recorded 5-bundle platform wave yet. Add generator validation, task-defined tests, and native output expectations for Pulumi YAML before running the verified wave.

immediateNextWork.label: Enable and run the verified 5-bundle wave for Ansible YAML
immediateNextWork.why: Ansible YAML has no complete recorded 5-bundle platform wave yet. Add generator validation and a real native output contract for Ansible before running the verified wave.

immediateNextWork.label: Make the complex adversarial runner platform-aware
immediateNextWork.why: The current complex runner is Pulumi TypeScript-only. Platform breadth should not depend on a misleading `--platform` flag unless the runner actually generates and validates those platforms.

waves.objective: Finish the services with official emulator leverage or storage-like data-plane behavior first, because they give the fastest path to high-fidelity integration tests.
